thread:
tim-oncall: incident-bot fired an alert for canary rollout r-20260315-17 — canary_5xx_rate ~6.2% (baseline ~0.3%), p95 latency jumped to 3210ms. Paging SRE oncall. Starting thread to coordinate. @mike-sre can you take?

deploy-bot: Deploy r-20260315-17 started 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z -> canary=10% (svc-model, svc-proxy)

mike-sre: on it. Looking at logs now. Early signal: memory spikes and OOM retries on canary model hosts causing retry loops -> 5xxs.

eva-eng: I see repeated "kv cache corrupt" warnings in model logs on the canary nodes around 10:12. Might be a compiled-kernel / quantization edge case that corrupts the KV cache.

tim-oncall: Customer impact: Support sees elevated error pages for a subset of EU customers — roughly 4% of API keys impacted. Need immediate mitigation: stop canary and drain traffic back to stable or flip feature flag to pin to v1. Which is faster?

sara-support: Confirmed two enterprise customers reported failed calls, one opened a P1 with CS. They want ETA.

mike-sre: fastest path is to kill canary routing at the traffic-router level. Plan: pause rollout, re-route canary to stable pool (soft drain), if still bad then revert model binary on canary nodes. I'll pause and start drain now.

tim-oncall: do it. I'll notify CS and post an incident note. Alex, can you handle customer comms?

alex-pm: on it — sending initial "we're investigating" to CS, will update every 30m or on significant progress.

mike-sre: Executing commands now:
```
# pause rollout
deployctl rollout pause r-20260315-17
# drain canary traffic to stable
routerctl set-weight svc-model canary 0 stable 100 --soft-drain
# check pods
kubectl -n inference get pods -l rollout=r-20260315-17 -o wide
```

deploy-bot: Rollout r-20260315-17: PAUSE requested by mike-sre @ 10:18:12Z

mike-sre: Drain in progress. Canary qps down from ~1200 -> ~80 over ~90s. Some pods still returning 5xx during drain, will forcibly kill after connection-drain window if needed.

eva-eng: If drain doesn't fully clear errors we should revert the model binary on the canary nodes. Revert command:
```
rbinctl revert svc-model --to v1.9-stable --nodes canary
```
Also prepare smoke test set.

tim-oncall: agreed. After revert, run smoke tests and report p95 + error rate. Targets: p95 < 250ms, error_rate < 0.1% on smoke queries.

mike-sre: reverting remaining problematic canary nodes now. Canary qps ~10, errors falling to 0.5%.

sara-support: CS updated — customers asking for ETA ~15m.

mike-sre: Revert completed on canary nodes. Restarting router to clear sticky sessions:
```
routerctl restart svc-model-router --reason "canary drain completed"
```
Running smoke suite (50 probes) against stable pool.

incident-bot: runbook excerpt: "If canary causes user-facing errors: pause rollout, drain traffic, revert canary artifacts, run smoke tests, escalate to Eng/SRE." https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollouts

mike-sre: Smoke results: 50/50 successful responses, 0 5xx, p95=180ms, error_rate=0.0%. Marking rollout state -> ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.

tim-oncall: Good work. Root cause hypothesis: compiled kernel selection mismatch produced KV cache corruption on quantized model path. Eva, please open a follow-up bug with logs, cores, and list of artifact hashes. Block further canaries until validated. Also add regression test for cache corruption.

eva-eng: Will open bug and start bisecting artifacts. Assigning to eng-inference. I'll attach log snippets and node core dumps.

alex-pm: CS updated: "Mitigated; ongoing investigation; follow-up within 2 business hours." :white_check_mark:

tim-oncall: handing off monitoring to mike-sre for the next 30m, then to oncall schedule. I'll add notes in PagerDuty and the incident ticket. Any concerns?

mike-sre: No concerns. I'll watch metrics and signal handoff when stable. :thumbsup:

-- end --
